Slice: Add Tool

Intent

Put a tool into the shed so neighbors can borrow it. The shed manager records the tool's name, an optional description, and its default checkout period. That period is the longest period a checkout of the tool can start with. A tool can be borrowed as soon as it is added: the Tool Catalog lists it as available (INV-TCAT-1), and Check Out Tool lends it.

Trigger & Actor

The shed manager, from the Tool Inventory screen, when a new physical item joins the shed. Each physical item is added on its own, including an item identical to one already in the shed.

Command / Input

Command: Add Tool

Field Type Required Rules / Validation
toolId ToolId yes A UUID chosen by the caller for the new tool, so a retried request is recognised. Must not belong to a different tool already added (INV-ADD-10).
name Text yes Leading and trailing whitespace (any Unicode whitespace) removed. Must not then be empty (INV-ADD-4). Need not be unique (INV-ADD-8).
description Text no Optional. Leading and trailing whitespace removed. Empty after that means none.
defaultCheckoutPeriodDays Int yes Whole days, 1 to 30 inclusive (INV-ADD-3). A fractional value is refused, never rounded.

Trigger

Triggered by: screen Tool Inventory @Shed Manager

Event(s) Emitted

Event: Tool Added → context Tools Read by: Tool Inventory and Tool Catalog (their own slices, right after this one); and, for the tool's name only, My Loans, My Holds, Overdue Loans To Notify, Undelivered Notices, Pickup Notices To Send and Flagged Neighbors.

Field Type Immutable Fact? Source / Notes
toolId ToolId yes From the command. Identifies the tool everywhere from here on.
name Text yes From the command, trimmed.
description Text yes Optional: absent when the command had none, or only whitespace. Otherwise from the command, trimmed.
defaultCheckoutPeriodDays Int yes From the command: whole days, 1 to 30.
addedAt Instant yes The UTC moment the event is recorded, set by the system.

Every field is fixed for good. No command changes a tool's name, description or default period; to correct a mistake, the shed manager retires the tool and adds it again.

Read Model / View

This slice produces no view of its own. Tool Added starts the new tool's entry in two views, each specified in its own doc:

  • Tool Inventory (slices/tool-inventory.md) lists the new tool for the shed manager.
  • Tool Catalog (slices/tool-catalog.md) lists it to neighbors as available to borrow.

Both are eventually consistent: the new tool appears once each view has caught up with Tool Added.

Invariants / Business Rules

  • INV-ADD-1: Only the shed manager can add a tool.
    • Neighbors do not add tools. How the shed manager is recognised is an open question below.
  • INV-ADD-2: Every tool is added with a default checkout period.
    • A checkout of this tool may start with a shorter period, never a longer one. An extension can later take a loan past it.
  • INV-ADD-3: A tool's default checkout period is a whole number of days, from 1 to 30.
  • INV-ADD-4: Every tool has a name. A description is optional.
    • A name that is empty, or only whitespace, is no name. A description that is empty, or only whitespace, is recorded as none.
  • INV-ADD-5: Each physical item is added as its own tool.
    • Two identical drills are two tools, each added separately. There is no quantity on a tool.
  • INV-ADD-8: Tool names need not be unique.
    • Two identical drills may both be named "Cordless drill". Each tool is told apart by its tool ID, not its name.
  • INV-ADD-9: Each tool gets its own tool ID when it is added, and keeps it for good.
    • The tool ID is how every later event, view and command refers to the tool. Names are only for people to read.
  • INV-ADD-10: Adding a tool with a tool ID that is already used adds nothing new.
    • A repeat with the same details, compared after trimming, succeeds and records nothing new, whatever has happened to the tool since. A repeat with different details is refused (tool-id-in-use).

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

  • Happy path
    • Given: the shed has no tools
    • When: the shed manager adds tool T1 named "Cordless drill", described as "18V, two batteries", with a default checkout period of 7 days, from the Tool Inventory screen
    • Then: Tool Added is recorded for T1 with that name, description and 7-day default checkout period, and the time it was added.
  • Tool added without a description (INV-ADD-4)
    • Given: the shed has no tools
    • When: the shed manager adds a tool named "Ladder" with a default checkout period of 3 days and no description
    • Then: Tool Added is recorded with that name, no description, and the 3-day period.
  • Blank description is no description (INV-ADD-4)
    • Given: the shed has no tools
    • When: the shed manager adds a tool named "Ladder" with a 3-day period and a description of only whitespace
    • Then: Tool Added is recorded with no description.
  • Whitespace around the name is removed (INV-ADD-4)
    • Given: the shed has no tools
    • When: the shed manager adds a tool named " Ladder " with a 3-day period
    • Then: Tool Added is recorded with the name "Ladder".
  • A second identical item (INV-ADD-5, INV-ADD-8, INV-ADD-9)
    • Given: the shed holds tool T1 named "Cordless drill"
    • When: the shed manager adds a second, identical drill as tool T2, also named "Cordless drill"
    • Then: Tool Added is recorded for T2, a separate tool with its own tool ID. The shed now has two tools named "Cordless drill", T1 and T2.
  • Shortest allowed period (INV-ADD-3)
    • Given: the shed has no tools
    • When: the shed manager adds a tool named "Stud finder" with a default checkout period of 1 day
    • Then: Tool Added is recorded with the 1-day period.
  • Longest allowed period (INV-ADD-3)
    • Given: the shed has no tools
    • When: the shed manager adds a tool named "Tile saw" with a default checkout period of 30 days
    • Then: Tool Added is recorded with the 30-day period.
  • Period over the maximum (INV-ADD-3)
    • Given: the shed has no tools
    • When: the shed manager tries to add a tool named "Tile saw" with a default checkout period of 31 days
    • Then: refused with period-out-of-range: "The default checkout period must be a whole number of days from 1 to 30." No event is recorded.
  • Period of zero (INV-ADD-3)
    • Given: the shed has no tools
    • When: the shed manager tries to add a tool with a default checkout period of 0 days
    • Then: refused with period-out-of-range: "The default checkout period must be a whole number of days from 1 to 30." No event is recorded.
  • Period that isn't a whole number of days (INV-ADD-3)
    • Given: the shed has no tools
    • When: the shed manager tries to add a tool with a default checkout period of 2.5 days
    • Then: refused with period-out-of-range: "The default checkout period must be a whole number of days from 1 to 30." No event is recorded.
  • No default period (INV-ADD-2)
    • Given: the shed has no tools
    • When: the shed manager tries to add a tool named "Ladder" with no default checkout period
    • Then: refused with period-missing: "A tool needs a default checkout period." No event is recorded.
  • No name (INV-ADD-4)
    • Given: the shed has no tools
    • When: the shed manager tries to add a tool whose name is empty, or only whitespace
    • Then: refused with name-missing: "A tool needs a name." No event is recorded.
  • Someone other than the shed manager tries to add a tool (INV-ADD-1)
    • Given: the request does not come from the shed manager
    • When: it asks to add a tool
    • Then: refused with not-shed-manager: "Only the shed manager can add tools." No event is recorded.
  • The same request arrives twice (INV-ADD-10)
    • Given: Tool Added was recorded for tool T1, "Cordless drill", 7 days
    • When: the same Add Tool request for T1, "Cordless drill", 7 days, arrives again
    • Then: the request succeeds and nothing new is recorded. The shed still has one tool T1.
  • The same request after the tool was retired (INV-ADD-10)
    • Given: Tool Added was recorded for tool T1, "Cordless drill", 7 days, and T1 has since been retired
    • When: the same Add Tool request for T1 arrives again
    • Then: the request succeeds and nothing new is recorded. T1 stays retired.
  • A repeat that differs only in whitespace (INV-ADD-10)
    • Given: Tool Added was recorded for tool T1, "Ladder", 3 days
    • When: an Add Tool request arrives for T1 named " Ladder ", 3 days
    • Then: the request succeeds and nothing new is recorded.
  • A tool ID reused for different details (INV-ADD-10)
    • Given: Tool Added was recorded for tool T1, "Cordless drill", 7 days
    • When: an Add Tool request arrives for T1 named "Ladder", 3 days
    • Then: refused with tool-id-in-use: "That tool ID is already used by another tool." No event is recorded.

Alternate & Error Flows

Every refusal records nothing and returns one reason: the stable name, and the sentence shown to the shed manager on the Tool Inventory screen. The name is the contract; the sentence is the required wording of the message.

Reason Sentence Rule
not-shed-manager Only the shed manager can add tools. INV-ADD-1
name-missing A tool needs a name. INV-ADD-4
period-missing A tool needs a default checkout period. INV-ADD-2
period-out-of-range The default checkout period must be a whole number of days from 1 to 30. INV-ADD-3
tool-id-in-use That tool ID is already used by another tool. INV-ADD-10

tool-id-in-use can only come from a faulty caller, not from the screen.

A missing or malformed tool ID (not a UUID) is bad input, rejected before any rule is checked. It is not a refusal and has no reason name.

Idempotency: a repeated request with the same tool ID and the same details, compared after trimming, succeeds and records nothing new, even if the tool has since been retired or lost. So a retry after a lost response never adds a second tool. Because identical items are legitimately added as separate tools (INV-ADD-5), a repeat is recognised by its tool ID only, never by matching names or details.

There are no retries, compensations or external calls in this slice.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: only the shed manager may add a tool (INV-ADD-1). How the shed manager is recognised is the identity question below.
  • PII & compliance: none. Tool Added holds only tool details, and doesn't record who added the tool.
  • Performance / SLA: none.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on: none. Add Tool is the first slice on the timeline. Refusing a reused tool ID needs only the earlier Tool Added events.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: Tool Inventory and Tool Catalog (a new entry); My Loans, My Holds, Overdue Loans To Notify, Undelivered Notices, Pickup Notices To Send and Flagged Neighbors (the tool's name). Check Out Tool and Place Hold act on the tool by its tool ID, and Check Out Tool takes the tool's default checkout period from it.

Open Questions

  • How does the system know that the person adding a tool is the shed manager?
    • No event or slice records who the shed manager is or how they sign in. Every shed-manager action (add, retire and mark tools lost; suspend and reinstate) depends on the answer.
    • (a) The shed manager has a sign-in set up outside the model, with a shed-manager role. Nothing about it is recorded as an event. (b) The shed manager is a neighbor account given a shed-manager role, which needs an event and slice to grant it.
    • Recommendation: (a). There is one shed manager, and nothing on record asks to change who it is.
  • Are there length limits on a tool's name and description?
    • Recommendation: name up to 100 characters, description up to 500. A longer one is refused with the limit in the reason, never cut short.
"},{"index":1,"name":"Check Out Tool","x0":264.25,"x1":408.25,"docHtml":"

Slice: Check Out Tool

Intent

Let a neighbor borrow a tool, self-service, from the Tool Catalog. The checkout opens a loan with a due date set from the tool's default checkout period, or from a shorter period the neighbor chooses. It is also how a holder collects a tool set aside for them: there is no separate pickup.

Trigger & Actor

The neighbor who will borrow the tool, from the Tool Catalog screen, on a tool the catalog offers Check Out on (available, reserved or set aside). The shed manager does not record checkouts. How the system recognises the neighbor is the open identity question in Add Tool (slices/add-tool.md); this slice follows its answer.

Command / Input

Command: Check Out Tool

A LoanId, ToolId or NeighborId is a UUID. One clock reading is taken when the command is handled. "Today" is that moment's calendar date in the shed's local time zone, and the event's checkedOutAt is that same moment.

Field Type Required Rules / Validation
loanId LoanId yes A UUID chosen by the caller for the new loan, so a retried request is recognised. Must not belong to a different loan already recorded (INV-CHK-12).
toolId ToolId yes The tool to borrow. Must be a tool that has been added (INV-CHK-11).
neighborId NeighborId yes The neighbor borrowing it, who must be the one making the request (INV-CHK-1). Must be a registered account (INV-CHK-11).
loanPeriodDays Int no Optional. Whole days, from 1 up to the tool's default checkout period (INV-CHK-6). When absent, the default applies. A fractional value is refused, never rounded.

Trigger

Triggered by: screen Tool Catalog @Neighbor

Event(s) Emitted

Event: Tool Checked Out → context Loans Read by: Tool Inventory, Tool Catalog and My Loans; My Holds, Holds To Fulfill, Pickups To Expire and Pickup Notices To Send (a holder's checkout ends their hold); Overdue Loans To Notify and Neighbors To Flag (the loan's due date); Undelivered Notices and Flagged Neighbors (loan details shown there).

Field Type Immutable Fact? Source / Notes
loanId LoanId yes From the command. Identifies the loan everywhere from here on.
toolId ToolId yes From the command.
neighborId NeighborId yes From the command: the borrower.
loanPeriodDays Int yes The period the loan started with: loanPeriodDays from the command, or the tool's default checkout period when it was absent.
dueDate Date yes Set by the system: the checkout date (today) plus loanPeriodDays. A later Loan Extended sets a new dueDate; this one never changes.
checkedOutAt Instant yes Set by the system: the UTC moment of the clock reading above. Its date in the shed's local time zone is the checkout date.

The event doesn't name the hold it ends. A holder has at most one hold on a tool, so readers match the ended hold by toolId and neighborId (INV-CHK-9).

Read Model / View

This slice produces no view of its own. Tool Checked Out changes the tool's entry in Tool Inventory and Tool Catalog, starts the loan's entry in My Loans, and ends the borrower's hold on the tool in My Holds and the hold to-do lists. Each view is specified in its own doc. All are eventually consistent.

Invariants / Business Rules

  • INV-CHK-1: A neighbor checks a tool out themselves, for themselves.
    • The command names the acting neighbor in neighborId, and the request must come from that neighbor (requester-mismatch otherwise). The shed manager does not record checkouts. How the requester is recognised is the open identity question.
  • INV-CHK-2: A tool that is already checked out can't be checked out again until it is returned or recorded lost.
    • A loan is open from Tool Checked Out until Tool Returned or Tool Lost for that loan.
  • INV-CHK-3: A tool set aside for a holder can be checked out only by that holder, until the end of the collect-by date.
    • A tool is set aside from Hold Fulfilled for a hold until that hold ends. The collect-by date is Hold Fulfilled.collectByDate, recorded on the event; this slice reads it and never works it out.
    • The holder's pickup is an ordinary checkout. There is no separate pickup event.
  • INV-CHK-3a: A tool that is back in the shed with holds waiting, and not set aside, can be checked out only by the neighbor whose hold is at the front of the queue.
    • This holds after a return before Hold Fulfilled is recorded, and after a set-aside ends before the next hold is fulfilled.
    • The front of the queue is the hold on the tool, still waiting, whose Hold Placed was recorded first. Queue order is the order the Hold Placed events were recorded, never a comparison of times.
  • INV-CHK-3b: A holder's claim on a set-aside tool ends at the start of the day after the collect-by date, shed local time, whether or not Hold Expired has been recorded yet.
    • From that moment the set-aside is treated as ended. If a hold is waiting, only the neighbor at the front of the queue can check the tool out (INV-CHK-3a), and the former holder is refused. If none is waiting, anyone can, the former holder included.
  • INV-CHK-4: A retired tool can't be checked out.
    • A tool recorded lost is retired by that, so it can't be checked out either.
  • INV-CHK-5: A neighbor with an overdue loan can't check out a tool.
    • A loan is overdue from the start of the day after its due date, in the shed's local time, while it is still open. The due date is the latest one set by Tool Checked Out or Loan Extended. Nothing records it; it is worked out from the due date and today.
    • Any open loan counts, including one whose tool has since been retired. A loan that ended because the tool was recorded lost no longer counts.
    • This also stops a holder collecting a tool set aside for them.
  • INV-CHK-6: The due date is set at checkout: the checkout date plus the loan period.
    • The loan period is the tool's default checkout period, unless the neighbor chooses a shorter one. It is never longer than the default.
    • A shorter period is chosen as a whole number of days, at least 1.
  • INV-CHK-7: A suspended neighbor can't check out a tool, and neither can a neighbor whose account is closed.
    • An account is suspended from Neighbor Suspended until Neighbor Reinstated, and closed for good from Neighbor Account Closed.
    • This also stops a suspended holder collecting a tool set aside for them. Their hold keeps its place, and the set-aside still lapses at the end of its collect-by date.
  • INV-CHK-8: There is no limit on how many tools one neighbor can have checked out at once.
  • INV-CHK-9: When a holder checks out the tool they hold, their hold ends, whether or not it had been fulfilled.
    • The tool is then on loan, so it is not set aside for anyone, and the next hold waits for its return. When the tool comes back, the former holder is no longer in the queue.
    • The views that show holds end it by matching the checkout's toolId and neighborId; a holder has at most one hold on a tool.
  • INV-CHK-11: The tool must have been added, and the borrower must be a registered account.
  • INV-CHK-12: Checking out with a loan ID that is already used opens no new loan.
    • A repeat with the same tool, borrower and loan period succeeds and records nothing new, whatever has happened to the loan since. A repeat with different details is refused.
    • The loan period compared is the one the loan started with: a request that leaves the period out is the same as one that sends the tool's default explicitly.

Check Out is offered on a reserved or set-aside tool to every neighbor, not only to the holder whose turn it is (Tool Catalog, INV-TCAT-11). This slice refuses anyone else with the reason (INV-CHK-3, INV-CHK-3a).

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

Unless a scenario says otherwise: the cordless drill (tool D) has a 7-day default checkout period, Ana, Ben and Cara are registered, active neighbors with no overdue loans, and today is 5 October.

  • Happy path (INV-CHK-6)
    • Given: the drill is available
    • When: Ana checks out the drill from the Tool Catalog as loan L1, keeping the default period
    • Then: Tool Checked Out is recorded for L1: the drill, Ana, a 7-day period, due 12 October, checked out today.
  • Shorter period chosen (INV-CHK-6)
    • Given: the drill is available
    • When: Ana checks out the drill and chooses a 3-day period
    • Then: Tool Checked Out is recorded with a 3-day period, due 8 October.
  • Shortest period (INV-CHK-6)
    • Given: the drill is available
    • When: Ana checks out the drill and chooses a 1-day period
    • Then: Tool Checked Out is recorded with a 1-day period, due 6 October.
  • Period equal to the default (INV-CHK-6)
    • Given: the drill is available
    • When: Ana checks out the drill and chooses a 7-day period
    • Then: Tool Checked Out is recorded with a 7-day period, due 12 October.
  • Period longer than the default (INV-CHK-6)
    • Given: the drill is available
    • When: Ana tries to check out the drill with an 8-day period
    • Then: refused with period-out-of-range: "The loan period must be a whole number of days from 1 up to this tool's default checkout period." No event is recorded.
  • Period of zero, or not whole (INV-CHK-6)
    • Given: the drill is available
    • When: Ana tries to check out the drill with a 0-day period, or a 2.5-day period
    • Then: refused with period-out-of-range: "The loan period must be a whole number of days from 1 up to this tool's default checkout period." No event is recorded.
  • Tool already checked out (INV-CHK-2)
    • Given: Ben has the drill on loan
    • When: Ana tries to check out the drill
    • Then: refused with tool-checked-out: "This tool is already checked out." No event is recorded.
  • Retired tool (INV-CHK-4)
    • Given: the drill has been retired
    • When: Ana tries to check out the drill
    • Then: refused with tool-retired: "This tool has been retired." No event is recorded.
  • Unknown tool (INV-CHK-11)
    • Given: no tool T9 has been added
    • When: Ana tries to check out T9
    • Then: refused with tool-not-found: "There is no such tool." No event is recorded.
  • Unknown neighbor (INV-CHK-11)
    • Given: no account N9 has been registered
    • When: a request to check out the drill for N9 arrives
    • Then: refused with neighbor-not-found: "There is no such neighbor." No event is recorded.
  • Suspended neighbor (INV-CHK-7)
    • Given: Ana is suspended, and the drill is available
    • When: Ana tries to check out the drill
    • Then: refused with neighbor-suspended: "You can't borrow tools while your account is suspended." No event is recorded.
  • Closed account (INV-CHK-7)
    • Given: Ana's account is closed
    • When: a request to check out the drill for Ana arrives
    • Then: refused with account-closed: "This account is closed." No event is recorded.
  • Reinstated neighbor can borrow again (INV-CHK-7)
    • Given: Ana was suspended and has been reinstated, and the drill is available
    • When: Ana checks out the drill
    • Then: Tool Checked Out is recorded for the drill and Ana.
  • Overdue loan blocks a checkout (INV-CHK-5)
    • Given: Ana has the ladder on loan, due 4 October, and the drill is available
    • When: Ana tries to check out the drill on 5 October
    • Then: refused with has-overdue-loan: "You have an overdue loan. Return it before borrowing another tool." No event is recorded.
  • A loan due today is not overdue (INV-CHK-5)
    • Given: Ana has the ladder on loan, due 5 October, and the drill is available
    • When: Ana checks out the drill on 5 October
    • Then: Tool Checked Out is recorded for the drill and Ana.
  • An extended loan is not overdue (INV-CHK-5)
    • Given: Ana's ladder loan was due 4 October, and Loan Extended moved it to 11 October
    • When: Ana checks out the drill on 5 October
    • Then: Tool Checked Out is recorded for the drill and Ana.
  • A loan ended by loss no longer blocks (INV-CHK-5)
    • Given: Ana's ladder loan was due 1 October, and Tool Lost has been recorded for it
    • When: Ana checks out the drill on 5 October
    • Then: Tool Checked Out is recorded for the drill and Ana.
  • Several loans at once (INV-CHK-8)
    • Given: Ana has the ladder and the hedge trimmer on loan, neither overdue, and the drill is available
    • When: Ana checks out the drill
    • Then: Tool Checked Out is recorded. Ana now has three tools on loan.
  • Holder collects a set-aside tool (INV-CHK-3, INV-CHK-9)
    • Given: Hold Fulfilled was recorded for Ben's hold on the drill with a collect-by date of 6 October, so the drill is set aside for him
    • When: Ben checks out the drill on 5 October
    • Then: Tool Checked Out is recorded for the drill and Ben, due 12 October. Ben's hold ends with it.
  • Holder collects on the collect-by date (INV-CHK-3)
    • Given: the drill is set aside for Ben, to collect by 5 October
    • When: Ben checks out the drill on 5 October
    • Then: Tool Checked Out is recorded for the drill and Ben.
  • Someone else tries to take a set-aside tool (INV-CHK-3)
    • Given: the drill is set aside for Ben, to collect by 6 October
    • When: Ana tries to check out the drill on 5 October
    • Then: refused with set-aside-for-another: "This tool is set aside for another neighbor." No event is recorded.
  • Overdue holder can't collect (INV-CHK-5)
    • Given: the drill is set aside for Ben, and Ben has the ladder on loan, due 2 October
    • When: Ben tries to check out the drill on 5 October
    • Then: refused with has-overdue-loan. The drill stays set aside for Ben until his collect-by date ends.
  • Suspended holder can't collect (INV-CHK-7)
    • Given: the drill is set aside for Ben, and Ben is suspended
    • When: Ben tries to check out the drill
    • Then: refused with neighbor-suspended. His hold keeps its place.
  • Front holder collects before the set-aside is recorded (INV-CHK-3a, INV-CHK-9)
    • Given: the drill has just been returned, Ben's hold is at the front of its queue and Cara's is behind it, and Hold Fulfilled has not yet been recorded
    • When: Ben checks out the drill
    • Then: Tool Checked Out is recorded for the drill and Ben. Ben's hold ends without ever being fulfilled.
  • An early collector is out of the queue when the tool returns (INV-CHK-9, INV-CHK-3a)
    • Given: Ben checked out the drill as the front holder before his hold was fulfilled, with Cara's hold behind his. He has since returned it, and Cara's hold is still waiting.
    • When: Ben tries to check out the drill again
    • Then: refused with reserved-for-another: "This tool is reserved for the next neighbor in the hold queue." No event is recorded. Cara is now at the front.
  • Someone who isn't next tries to take a reserved tool (INV-CHK-3a)
    • Given: the drill has just been returned, with Ben's hold at the front and Cara's behind it, and Hold Fulfilled has not yet been recorded
    • When: Cara tries to check out the drill, and then Ana does
    • Then: both are refused with reserved-for-another: "This tool is reserved for the next neighbor in the hold queue." No event is recorded.
  • Holder too late, another hold waiting (INV-CHK-3b)
    • Given: the drill was set aside for Ben on 14 October, to collect by 17 October, and Cara's hold is waiting. Hold Expired has not yet been recorded.
    • When: Ben tries to check out the drill on 18 October
    • Then: refused with pickup-window-ended: "Your pickup window has ended, and this tool has passed to the next neighbor in the queue." No event is recorded. Cara can check the drill out.
  • Someone else tries a lapsed set-aside while a hold waits (INV-CHK-3a, INV-CHK-3b)
    • Given: as above, on 18 October, before Hold Expired is recorded
    • When: Ana, who has no hold on the drill, tries to check it out
    • Then: refused with reserved-for-another. No event is recorded.
  • Next holder takes a lapsed set-aside before the expiry is recorded (INV-CHK-3a, INV-CHK-3b)
    • Given: as above, on 18 October, before Hold Expired is recorded
    • When: Cara checks out the drill
    • Then: Tool Checked Out is recorded for the drill and Cara, and her hold ends. Ben's hold still gets its Hold Expired.
  • Lapsed set-aside, no hold waiting, taken by someone else (INV-CHK-3b)
    • Given: the drill was set aside for Ben, to collect by 17 October, no other hold is waiting, and Hold Expired has not yet been recorded
    • When: Ana checks out the drill on 18 October
    • Then: Tool Checked Out is recorded for the drill and Ana. Ben's hold still gets its Hold Expired.
  • Lapsed set-aside, no hold waiting, taken by the former holder (INV-CHK-3b, INV-CHK-9)
    • Given: as above
    • When: Ben checks out the drill on 18 October
    • Then: Tool Checked Out is recorded for the drill and Ben. His own checkout ends his hold, so no Hold Expired follows for it.
  • The same request arrives twice (INV-CHK-12)
    • Given: Tool Checked Out was recorded for loan L1: the drill, Ana, default period
    • When: the same Check Out Tool request for L1 arrives again
    • Then: the request succeeds and nothing new is recorded. Ana still has one loan of the drill.
  • A loan ID reused for different details (INV-CHK-12)
    • Given: Tool Checked Out was recorded for loan L1: the drill, Ana
    • When: a Check Out Tool request for L1 arrives naming the ladder
    • Then: refused with loan-id-in-use: "That loan ID is already used by another loan." No event is recorded.
  • Someone checks out a tool for another neighbor (INV-CHK-1)
    • Given: the drill is available
    • When: a request to check out the drill for Ana comes from someone other than Ana
    • Then: refused with requester-mismatch: "You can only check out tools for yourself." No event is recorded.

Alternate & Error Flows

Every refusal records nothing and returns one reason: the stable name, and the sentence shown to the neighbor on the Tool Catalog screen. The name is the contract; the sentence is the required wording of the message.

The checks run in this order, and the first that fails is the reason returned:

  1. requester-mismatch (INV-CHK-1).
  2. The loan ID is already used (INV-CHK-12): a repeat with the same details succeeds with nothing recorded; otherwise loan-id-in-use.
  3. tool-not-found, then neighbor-not-found (INV-CHK-11).
  4. tool-retired (INV-CHK-4).
  5. tool-checked-out (INV-CHK-2).
  6. account-closed, then neighbor-suspended (INV-CHK-7).
  7. has-overdue-loan (INV-CHK-5).
  8. The tool's holds (INV-CHK-3, INV-CHK-3a, INV-CHK-3b):
    • set-aside-for-another: the tool is set aside and its collect-by date hasn't ended, and the requester isn't the holder.
    • pickup-window-ended: the set-aside's collect-by date has ended, another hold is waiting, and the requester is the former holder.
    • reserved-for-another: the tool is back with a hold waiting (or a lapsed set-aside with one waiting), and the requester isn't the neighbor at the front of the queue. This includes a third neighbor after a set-aside lapses.
  9. period-out-of-range (INV-CHK-6).
Reason Sentence Rule
loan-id-in-use That loan ID is already used by another loan. INV-CHK-12
requester-mismatch You can only check out tools for yourself. INV-CHK-1
tool-not-found There is no such tool. INV-CHK-11
neighbor-not-found There is no such neighbor. INV-CHK-11
tool-retired This tool has been retired. INV-CHK-4
tool-checked-out This tool is already checked out. INV-CHK-2
account-closed This account is closed. INV-CHK-7
neighbor-suspended You can't borrow tools while your account is suspended. INV-CHK-7
has-overdue-loan You have an overdue loan. Return it before borrowing another tool. INV-CHK-5
set-aside-for-another This tool is set aside for another neighbor. INV-CHK-3
pickup-window-ended Your pickup window has ended, and this tool has passed to the next neighbor in the queue. INV-CHK-3b
reserved-for-another This tool is reserved for the next neighbor in the hold queue. INV-CHK-3a
period-out-of-range The loan period must be a whole number of days from 1 up to this tool's default checkout period. INV-CHK-6

loan-id-in-use, tool-not-found and neighbor-not-found can only come from a faulty caller, not from the screen. A missing or malformed ID (not a UUID) is bad input, rejected before any rule is checked. It is not a refusal and has no reason name.

Idempotency: a repeated request with the same loan ID and the same tool, borrower and requested period succeeds and records nothing new, even if the loan has since been extended, returned or lost. So a retry after a lost response never opens a second loan.

Two neighbors checking out the same tool at the same moment: only one Tool Checked Out is recorded for the tool. The other request is refused with tool-checked-out, because each checkout is decided against the tool's loans as already recorded, one at a time.

There are no external calls, retries or compensations in this slice.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: a neighbor may check out a tool only for themselves (INV-CHK-1); the shed manager doesn't check tools out. How the requester is recognised is the open identity question in Add Tool.
  • PII & compliance: Tool Checked Out links a neighbor to a tool and a due date. It holds no name or email; those stay on Neighbor Registered and Neighbor Email Changed.
  • Performance / SLA: none beyond the one-at-a-time rule above.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, to apply its rules, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Tool Added (Add Tool): toolId, defaultCheckoutPeriodDays.
    • Tool Retired (Retire Tool): toolId.
    • Tool Lost (Record Tool Lost): loanId.
    • Tool Checked Out (this slice): loanId, toolId, neighborId, loanPeriodDays, dueDate.
    • Loan Extended (Extend Loan): loanId, dueDate.
    • Tool Returned (Return Tool): loanId.
    • Neighbor Registered (Register Neighbor): neighborId.
    • Neighbor Suspended (Suspend Neighbor), Neighbor Reinstated (Reinstate Neighbor), Neighbor Account Closed (Close Account): neighborId.
    • Hold Placed (Place Hold): holdId, toolId, neighborId. Queue order is the order these events were recorded.
    • Hold Fulfilled (Fulfill Hold): holdId, collectByDate.
    • Hold Cancelled (Cancel Hold), Hold Expired (Expire Hold): holdId.
    • These keys match slices/add-tool.md, tool-inventory.md, tool-catalog.md and register-neighbor.md. Hold Fulfilled.collectByDate is the Date the fulfiller records (set by the system, as dueDate is on loans). Those slices aren't yet written in depth, and each is checked against these keys when it is.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: Tool Inventory, Tool Catalog, My Loans, My Holds, Overdue Loans To Notify, Undelivered Notices, Holds To Fulfill, Pickup Notices To Send, Pickups To Expire, Neighbors To Flag and Flagged Neighbors. Extend Loan, Return Tool and Record Tool Lost act on the loan by its loan ID.

Open Questions

None.

"},{"index":2,"name":"Place Hold","x0":433.25,"x1":577.25,"docHtml":"

Slice: Place Hold

Intent

Let a neighbor get in line for a tool that isn't available to borrow right now, by placing a hold from the Tool Catalog. Holds on a tool are fulfilled in the order they were placed: when the tool is back in the shed, it is set aside for the neighbor at the front of the queue.

Trigger & Actor

A neighbor, from the Tool Catalog, on a tool that is checked out, set aside for a holder, or reserved (back in the shed with holds waiting, not yet set aside). The catalog is the same for every neighbor, so it offers Place Hold on every such tool to everyone; a neighbor who may not hold it is refused with a reason they can see. The shed manager doesn't place holds.

Command / Input

Command: Place Hold

A HoldId, ToolId or NeighborId is a UUID.

Field Type Required Rules / Validation
holdId HoldId yes A UUID chosen by the caller for the new hold, so a retried request is recognised. Must not belong to a different hold already placed (INV-HOLD-13).
toolId ToolId yes The tool to hold. Must be a tool that has been added (INV-HOLD-14), not retired (INV-HOLD-3), and not available (INV-HOLD-2).
neighborId NeighborId yes The neighbor placing the hold, who must be the one making the request (INV-HOLD-1). Must be a registered account (INV-HOLD-14), not closed (INV-HOLD-4) and not suspended (INV-HOLD-9).

Trigger

Triggered by: screen Tool Catalog @Neighbor

Event(s) Emitted

Event: Hold Placed → context Holds Read by: My Holds (its own slice, which shows the neighbor their place in the queue), Tool Catalog (holds waiting, and a tool's status), My Loans (a hold waiting on a borrowed tool), and Holds To Fulfill (the queue the hold fulfiller works from).

Field Type Immutable Fact? Source / Notes
holdId HoldId yes From the command. Identifies the hold everywhere from here on.
toolId ToolId yes From the command.
neighborId NeighborId yes From the command: the holder.
placedAt Instant yes The UTC moment the event is recorded, set by the system. For display only: the queue is the order Hold Placed is recorded, since two holds can share a timestamp.

Every field is fixed for good. A hold's later life (fulfilled, cancelled, expired, ended) is recorded by other events; nothing changes Hold Placed.

Read Model / View

This slice produces no view of its own. Hold Placed feeds four views, each specified in its own doc:

  • My Holds (slices/my-holds.md) shows the neighbor the new hold and its place in the queue.
  • Tool Catalog (slices/tool-catalog.md) counts it among the holds waiting on the tool.
  • My Loans (slices/my-loans.md) shows the borrower of the tool that someone is waiting.
  • Holds To Fulfill (slices/holds-to-fulfill.md) adds it to the tool's queue.

All are eventually consistent: the hold shows once each view has caught up with Hold Placed.

Invariants / Business Rules

A tool's state, for these rules, is tested against its events as already recorded, in this order; the first that holds wins:

  1. checked-out — a loan of the tool is open: Tool Checked Out recorded, and neither Tool Returned nor Tool Lost for that loan.
  2. set-aside — otherwise, a hold on the tool has been fulfilled and hasn't ended.
  3. reserved — otherwise, at least one hold on the tool is waiting.
  4. available — otherwise.

This is the same test the Tool Catalog uses for a tool's status.

A hold is waiting from Hold Placed until it is fulfilled or ends. A hold ends when it is cancelled or expires, when the holder checks the tool out, when the tool is retired or recorded lost, or when the holder closes their account. Once fulfilled, the tool is set aside for the holder until the end of the collect-by date, the set-aside date plus 3 days; a set-aside whose collect-by date has passed still counts as set aside until Hold Expired is recorded for it. Other slices record these endings; this slice reads them.

The Tool Catalog is the same for every neighbor, so it offers Place Hold on every tool that isn't available and can't hide the action from a neighbor who may not use it. Each rule below that refuses a neighbor (INV-HOLD-4, INV-HOLD-7, INV-HOLD-8, INV-HOLD-9) does so with a reason the neighbor can see.

  • INV-HOLD-1: A neighbor places a hold themselves, from the Tool Catalog, and only for themselves.
    • The neighbor ID must be the neighbor making the request. How the requester is recognised is the open identity question below.
  • INV-HOLD-2: A hold can be placed on any tool that isn't available.
    • That is a tool that is checked out, set aside for a holder, or back in the shed with holds waiting but not yet set aside.
    • A hold on an available tool is refused. The neighbor checks it out instead.
  • INV-HOLD-3: A hold can't be placed on a retired tool.
    • A tool recorded lost is retired by that. Retiring a tool ends every hold on it.
  • INV-HOLD-4: A neighbor whose account is closed can't place a hold.
    • Closing an account ends all of that neighbor's holds.
  • INV-HOLD-5: A new hold joins the back of the tool's queue.
    • The order is the order Hold Placed events are recorded for the tool. placedAt is for display only, since two holds can share a timestamp. Holds on one tool are decided one at a time, so no two share a place.
    • Holds are fulfilled in queue order; that is Fulfill Hold's rule (INV-FUL-2).
  • INV-HOLD-7: A neighbor can have only one hold on a given tool.
    • A second hold by the same neighbor on the same tool is refused, whether their first hold is waiting or set aside.
    • A hold that has ended doesn't count. After cancelling, or once their hold has expired, the neighbor may hold the tool again, at the back of the queue.
  • INV-HOLD-8: A neighbor can't place a hold on a tool they have on loan themselves.
  • INV-HOLD-9: A suspended neighbor can't place a new hold.
    • Holds they placed before the suspension keep their place in the queue.
  • INV-HOLD-10: A neighbor with an overdue loan may place a hold.
    • The overdue loan stops them collecting the tool if it is set aside for them (Check Out Tool, INV-CHK-5), not placing the hold.
  • INV-HOLD-11: There is no limit on how many holds one neighbor can have at once.
  • INV-HOLD-13: Placing a hold with a hold ID that is already used places no new hold.
    • A repeat with the same tool and neighbor succeeds and records nothing new, whatever has happened to the hold since. A repeat with a different tool or neighbor is refused (hold-id-in-use).
  • INV-HOLD-14: The tool must have been added, and the neighbor must be a registered account.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

  • Happy path: first hold on a checked-out tool (INV-HOLD-2, INV-HOLD-5)
    • Given: Ana (N1) has the cordless drill (T1) on loan, due 12 October, and no holds are waiting on it. Ben (N2) is active.
    • When: Ben places hold H1 on T1 from the Tool Catalog
    • Then: Hold Placed is recorded for H1: T1, N2, and the time it was placed.
  • Second hold queues behind the first (INV-HOLD-5)
    • Given: T1 is checked out, and Ben's hold H1 on it is waiting
    • When: Cleo (N3) places hold H2 on T1
    • Then: Hold Placed is recorded for H2, after H1. H2 is behind H1 in T1's queue.
  • Hold on a set-aside tool (INV-HOLD-2)
    • Given: T1 was returned and is set aside for Ben's hold H1, and no other hold is waiting
    • When: Cleo places hold H2 on T1
    • Then: Hold Placed is recorded for H2, behind Ben's set-aside.
  • Hold on a reserved tool (INV-HOLD-2)
    • Given: T1 has just been returned, Ben's hold H1 is waiting, and Hold Fulfilled has not yet been recorded
    • When: Cleo places hold H2 on T1
    • Then: Hold Placed is recorded for H2, behind H1.
  • Available tool (INV-HOLD-2)
    • Given: the ladder (T2) is in the shed with no holds
    • When: Ben tries to place a hold on T2
    • Then: refused with tool-available: "This tool is available. Check it out instead." No event is recorded.
  • Retired tool (INV-HOLD-3)
    • Given: T1 was retired while Ana had it on loan
    • When: Ben tries to place a hold on T1
    • Then: refused with tool-retired: "This tool has been retired." No event is recorded.
  • Already holding this tool (INV-HOLD-7)
    • Given: T1 is checked out, and Ben's hold H1 on it is waiting
    • When: Ben tries to place hold H3 on T1
    • Then: refused with already-holding: "You already have a hold on this tool." No event is recorded.
  • Already holding this tool, set aside for them (INV-HOLD-7)
    • Given: T1 is set aside for Ben's hold H1
    • When: Ben tries to place hold H3 on T1
    • Then: refused with already-holding: "You already have a hold on this tool." No event is recorded.
  • Holding again after cancelling (INV-HOLD-7)
    • Given: T1 is checked out, Ben's hold H1 on it was cancelled, and Cleo's hold H2 is waiting
    • When: Ben places hold H4 on T1
    • Then: Hold Placed is recorded for H4, behind H2.
  • Holding again after expiry (INV-HOLD-7)
    • Given: T1 was set aside for Ben's hold H1, Hold Expired was recorded for H1, and Cleo now has T1 on loan
    • When: Ben places hold H5 on T1
    • Then: Hold Placed is recorded for H5.
  • Tool on loan to the neighbor (INV-HOLD-8)
    • Given: Ana has T1 on loan
    • When: Ana tries to place a hold on T1
    • Then: refused with tool-on-loan-to-you: "You have this tool on loan." No event is recorded.
  • Suspended neighbor (INV-HOLD-9)
    • Given: T1 is checked out by Ana, and Ben is suspended
    • When: Ben tries to place a hold on T1
    • Then: refused with neighbor-suspended: "You can't place holds while your account is suspended." No event is recorded.
  • Closed account (INV-HOLD-4)
    • Given: T1 is checked out by Ana, and Ben's account is closed
    • When: a hold on T1 is requested for Ben
    • Then: refused with account-closed: "This account is closed." No event is recorded.
  • Neighbor with an overdue loan (INV-HOLD-10)
    • Given: Ben has the ladder on loan, overdue, and Ana has T1 on loan
    • When: Ben places hold H6 on T1
    • Then: Hold Placed is recorded for H6.
  • Holds on several tools (INV-HOLD-11)
    • Given: Ben's hold H1 on T1 is waiting, and the hedge trimmer (T3) is checked out by Ana
    • When: Ben places hold H7 on T3
    • Then: Hold Placed is recorded for H7. Ben now has holds on T1 and T3.
  • A hold for someone else (INV-HOLD-1)
    • Given: T1 is checked out by Ana
    • When: a request from Ben asks to place a hold on T1 for Cleo
    • Then: refused with requester-mismatch: "You can only place holds for yourself." No event is recorded.
  • Unknown tool (INV-HOLD-14)
    • Given: no tool has ID T9
    • When: Ben asks to place a hold on T9
    • Then: refused with tool-not-found: "There is no such tool." No event is recorded.
  • Unknown neighbor (INV-HOLD-14)
    • Given: T1 is checked out by Ana, and no account has neighbor ID N9
    • When: a hold on T1 is requested for N9
    • Then: refused with neighbor-not-found: "There is no such neighbor." No event is recorded.
  • Hold on a lapsed set-aside (INV-HOLD-2)
    • Given: T1 was set aside for Ben's hold H1, collect by 17 October, and Hold Expired hasn't been recorded for H1
    • When: on 18 October, Cleo places hold H8 on T1
    • Then: Hold Placed is recorded for H8. T1 still counts as set aside, not available.
  • Lapsed holder holds again before expiry (INV-HOLD-7)
    • Given: T1 was set aside for Ben's hold H1, collect by 17 October, and Hold Expired hasn't been recorded for H1
    • When: on 18 October, Ben tries to place hold H9 on T1
    • Then: refused with already-holding: "You already have a hold on this tool." No event is recorded. Once Hold Expired is recorded for H1, he may hold T1 again.
  • The same request arrives twice (INV-HOLD-13)
    • Given: Hold Placed was recorded for H1: T1, Ben
    • When: the same Place Hold request for H1, T1, Ben arrives again
    • Then: the request succeeds and nothing new is recorded. Ben still has one hold on T1.
  • The same request after the hold ended (INV-HOLD-13)
    • Given: Hold Placed was recorded for H1: T1, Ben, and H1 has since been cancelled
    • When: the same Place Hold request for H1 arrives again
    • Then: the request succeeds and nothing new is recorded. H1 stays cancelled.
  • A hold ID reused for a different hold (INV-HOLD-13)
    • Given: Hold Placed was recorded for H1: T1, Ben
    • When: a Place Hold request arrives for H1 with T3, Ben
    • Then: refused with hold-id-in-use: "That hold ID is already used by another hold." No event is recorded.

Alternate & Error Flows

Every refusal records nothing and returns one reason: the stable name, and the sentence shown to the neighbor on the Tool Catalog screen. The name is the contract; the sentence is the required wording of the message.

The checks run in this order, and the first that fails is the reason returned:

  1. requester-mismatch (INV-HOLD-1): who is asking is settled before anything else.
  2. The hold ID is already used (INV-HOLD-13): a repeat with the same details succeeds with nothing recorded; otherwise hold-id-in-use.
  3. tool-not-found, then neighbor-not-found (INV-HOLD-14).
  4. tool-retired (INV-HOLD-3).
  5. account-closed, then neighbor-suspended (INV-HOLD-4, INV-HOLD-9).
  6. tool-on-loan-to-you (INV-HOLD-8).
  7. already-holding (INV-HOLD-7).
  8. tool-available (INV-HOLD-2).
Reason Sentence Rule
hold-id-in-use That hold ID is already used by another hold. INV-HOLD-13
requester-mismatch You can only place holds for yourself. INV-HOLD-1
tool-not-found There is no such tool. INV-HOLD-14
neighbor-not-found There is no such neighbor. INV-HOLD-14
tool-retired This tool has been retired. INV-HOLD-3
account-closed This account is closed. INV-HOLD-4
neighbor-suspended You can't place holds while your account is suspended. INV-HOLD-9
tool-on-loan-to-you You have this tool on loan. INV-HOLD-8
already-holding You already have a hold on this tool. INV-HOLD-7
tool-available This tool is available. Check it out instead. INV-HOLD-2

hold-id-in-use, tool-not-found and neighbor-not-found can only come from a faulty caller, not from the screen. A missing or malformed ID (not a UUID) is bad input, rejected before any rule is checked. It is not a refusal and has no reason name. The names and sentences shared with Check Out Tool (tool-not-found, neighbor-not-found, tool-retired, account-closed) are worded the same there.

Idempotency: a repeated request with the same hold ID, tool and neighbor succeeds and records nothing new, even if the hold has since been fulfilled, cancelled, expired or ended. So a retry after a lost response never places a second hold.

Requests at the same moment: each Place Hold is decided against the tool's holds and loans as already recorded, one at a time per tool. Two neighbors holding the same tool together are both recorded, in the order they are decided. The same neighbor sending two holds on one tool together gets one recorded; the other is refused with already-holding.

A set-aside past its collect-by date still counts as set aside until Hold Expired is recorded for it. Until then the tool is not available, so a hold on it is accepted (INV-HOLD-2), and the lapsed holder's own hold still counts as theirs (INV-HOLD-7).

There are no external calls, retries or compensations in this slice. Placing a hold sends no email.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: a neighbor may place a hold only for themselves (INV-HOLD-1); the shed manager doesn't place holds. How the requester is recognised is the open identity question below.
  • PII & compliance: Hold Placed links a neighbor to a tool. It holds no name or email; those stay on Neighbor Registered and Neighbor Email Changed.
  • Performance / SLA: none beyond the one-at-a-time rule above.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, to apply its rules, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Tool Added (Add Tool): toolId.
    • Tool Retired (Retire Tool): toolId.
    • Tool Lost (Record Tool Lost): loanId.
    • Tool Checked Out (Check Out Tool): loanId, toolId, neighborId.
    • Tool Returned (Return Tool): loanId.
    • Hold Placed (this slice): holdId, toolId, neighborId.
    • Hold Fulfilled (Fulfill Hold): holdId.
    • Hold Cancelled (Cancel Hold): holdId.
    • Hold Expired (Expire Hold): holdId.
    • Neighbor Registered (Register Neighbor): neighborId.
    • Neighbor Suspended (Suspend Neighbor): neighborId.
    • Neighbor Reinstated (Reinstate Neighbor): neighborId.
    • Neighbor Account Closed (Close Account): neighborId.
    • These keys match slices/add-tool.md, slices/register-neighbor.md, slices/check-out-tool.md, slices/tool-inventory.md and slices/tool-catalog.md. The others are specified in slices not yet written in depth; each is checked against these keys when it is.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: My Holds, Tool Catalog, My Loans and Holds To Fulfill (the new hold). Fulfill Hold sets the tool aside for the front of the queue; Cancel Hold, Expire Hold, Check Out Tool, Retire Tool, Record Tool Lost and Close Account end holds; Extend Loan refuses while a hold is waiting.

Open Questions

  • How does the system know which neighbor is placing the hold?
    • The same identity question is open in Add Tool, Register Neighbor, My Account and My Loans.
    • Options: (a) callers say who they are, and nothing checks it; (b) a sign-in outside the model supplies the neighbor's ID; (c) sign-in is modeled as events and slices.
    • Recommendation: (b), which adds nothing to the model.
"},{"index":3,"name":"My Holds","x0":602.25,"x1":746.25,"docHtml":"

Slice: My Holds

Intent

Shows a neighbor the holds they have, on the My Holds screen: where they stand in each tool's queue, and when a tool has been set aside for them, the date to collect it by and whether the pickup email reached them. It is the only screen that tells a neighbor a tool is waiting for them, and the screen they cancel holds from.

Trigger & Actor

  • Actor: a neighbor, opening their own My Holds screen.
  • Whose holds it shows: the holds of the neighbor asking. How the system knows who is asking is the open identity question below; this view answers for whichever neighbor ID that supplies.
  • Actions offered: nothing on this screen records anything by itself. Its one action issues a command owned by another slice:
    • Cancel (Cancel Hold slice) — offered on every listed hold (INV-MYHD-16).
    • A neighbor collects a set-aside tool with an ordinary checkout from the Tool Catalog, not from here.

Read Model / View

  • View: My Holds built from events: "Hold Placed", "Tool Checked Out", "Tool Added", "Hold Cancelled", "Hold Fulfilled", "Pickup Notice Sent", "Pickup Notice Failed", "Hold Expired", "Tool Retired", "Tool Lost", "Neighbor Account Closed"
  • Consumed by: the My Holds screen (Neighbor)
  • Freshness / consistency expectation: eventual for everything that comes from events: a change shows shortly after its event is recorded (seconds, not minutes). Whether a set-aside's pickup window has ended is worked out when the view is read, from collectByDate and today's date in the shed's local time zone, so it is always current. No action on this screen depends on the view being instant, because Cancel Hold and Check Out Tool each check their own rules when they run.

One row per hold that hasn't ended. HoldId, ToolId, LoanId and NeighborId are UUIDs. A Date is a calendar date in the shed's local time zone; an Instant is a UTC instant set when the event was recorded. A field marked optional can be absent.

Field Type Source / Notes
holdId HoldId Hold Placed.holdId.
neighborId NeighborId Hold Placed.neighborId: the holder.
toolId ToolId Hold Placed.toolId.
toolName Text Derived: Tool Added.name for toolId, copied under this name (INV-MYHD-14).
placedAt Instant Hold Placed.placedAt. For display only; it doesn't decide the queue.
status Text One of waiting, ready-for-pickup, pickup-window-ended. Derived: see the status rules below.
position Int Derived: while status is waiting, 1 plus the number of this tool's holds that are waiting, were placed before this one, and haven't ended (INV-MYHD-2). Optional: absent once the hold is fulfilled.
collectByDate Date Derived: Hold Fulfilled.collectByDate for this hold, read as recorded, never worked out here (INV-MYHD-3). Optional: absent while waiting.
pickupNotice Text One of none, sent, undelivered. Derived: sent once Pickup Notice Sent is recorded for this hold, undelivered once Pickup Notice Failed is recorded for it, none before either (INV-MYHD-13).
canCancel Bool Derived: yes on every listed hold (INV-MYHD-16).

Status rules. A hold's status is a test of its current facts, taken in this order. The first that holds wins:

  1. pickup-window-ended — Hold Fulfilled has been recorded for the hold, and today's date in the shed's local time zone is after its collectByDate (INV-MYHD-17).
  2. ready-for-pickup — otherwise, Hold Fulfilled has been recorded for the hold.
  3. waiting — otherwise.

When a hold leaves the view. A hold is listed from Hold Placed until it ends. A hold ends when it is cancelled or expires, when the holder checks the tool out, when the tool is retired or recorded lost, or when the holder closes their account. In events:

  • Hold Cancelled or Hold Expired for the hold;
  • Tool Checked Out for the hold's tool by the hold's neighbor;
  • Tool Retired or Tool Lost for the hold's tool;
  • Neighbor Account Closed for the holder.

Queue order. A tool's queue is the order in which Hold Placed was recorded for it. To work out positions, the view keeps, for each tool, every hold on it that hasn't ended, with its holder and whether it has been fulfilled. This is bookkeeping, not part of the row, and other neighbors' holds are never returned.

Queries

  • List my holds. Takes the asking neighbor's neighborId. Returns every hold of that neighbor that hasn't ended, each with every field above, and nothing about anyone else's holds (INV-MYHD-1). There is no paging. A neighbor with no holds gets an empty list. The order is an open question below.

Invariants / Business Rules

A neighbor has at most one hold on any one tool, because Place Hold refuses a second (INV-HOLD-7, Place Hold). A suspended neighbor can't place a new hold (INV-HOLD-9) or collect a set-aside tool (INV-CHK-7), but may still cancel. An expired hold sends no message, doesn't count against the neighbor, and the neighbor may place a new hold on the tool at the back of the queue (Expire Hold, INV-EXP-7 to INV-EXP-9). A suspended neighbor keeps their holds and their place in each queue. A front holder who can't collect, because they are suspended or have an overdue loan, still has the tool set aside for them, and the pickup window runs regardless (Fulfill Hold, INV-FUL-8). These rules are owned by those slices; this view just reflects the events they record, and it doesn't hear suspension or loans at all (INV-MYHD-11).

  • INV-MYHD-1: A neighbor's My Holds shows only their own holds.
    • The query returns only holds whose holder is the neighbor ID it is given. It never shows who else holds a tool, only the neighbor's own position; whether any neighbor-facing screen shows that is the open question in Tool Catalog (slices/tool-catalog.md) about showing who has a tool.
  • INV-MYHD-2: Holds on a tool queue in the order they were placed. Each waiting hold shows the neighbor's position in that tool's queue.
    • Position 1 is the next hold to be fulfilled. A hold moves up as holds ahead of it are fulfilled or end.
    • A hold that has been fulfilled is no longer in the waiting queue, so the first waiting hold behind a set-aside is at position 1.
  • INV-MYHD-3: Once a neighbor's hold is fulfilled, My Holds shows the tool as ready for pickup, with the date to collect it by.
    • The collect-by date is the one Hold Fulfilled carries: the date the tool was set aside plus 3 days. My Holds shows it as recorded and never works it out itself.
    • My Holds is the only screen that tells a neighbor a tool is set aside for them. The Tool Catalog is the same for every neighbor.
  • INV-MYHD-4: A hold that is ready for pickup stays on My Holds until the holder collects it, cancels it, or Hold Expired is recorded for it. Then it drops off.
    • The tool then passes to the next hold, which shows as ready for pickup on that neighbor's My Holds once Hold Fulfilled is recorded for it.
  • INV-MYHD-5: When a holder checks out the tool they hold, their hold ends and drops off My Holds, whether or not it had been fulfilled.
    • The loan then appears on My Loans.
  • INV-MYHD-6: A cancelled hold drops off My Holds, whether it was waiting or ready for pickup.
    • Cancelling a hold that is ready for pickup passes the tool to the next hold, the same as expiry.
  • INV-MYHD-7: Retiring a tool, or recording it lost, ends every hold on it, and those holds drop off My Holds.
    • The holders are not told.
  • INV-MYHD-8: Closing an account ends all of that neighbor's holds. Their holds drop off My Holds, and holds behind them move up.
    • A tool that was ready for pickup for them passes to the next hold, the same as expiry.
  • INV-MYHD-13: Once a tool is set aside for a neighbor, My Holds shows whether the pickup email was sent or couldn't be delivered.
    • If the email can't be delivered, the tool stays ready for pickup, with the same collect-by date.
  • INV-MYHD-14: Each hold shows the tool's name.
    • The name comes from Tool Added, which My Holds hears for that purpose.
  • INV-MYHD-11: Only Hold Placed, Hold Cancelled, Hold Fulfilled, Pickup Notice Sent, Pickup Notice Failed, Hold Expired, Tool Checked Out by a holder of that tool, Tool Retired, Tool Lost and Neighbor Account Closed change My Holds. Tool Added supplies tool names.
    • A checkout by anyone else leaves every neighbor's My Holds unchanged.
  • INV-MYHD-15: Applying the same event twice leaves My Holds as if it had been applied once.
  • INV-MYHD-16: My Holds offers Cancel on every hold it lists.
    • That includes holds ready for pickup, holds whose pickup window has ended, and holds of a suspended neighbor.
  • INV-MYHD-17: Once a set-aside's collect-by date has passed, My Holds shows that the pickup window has ended, even before Hold Expired is recorded.
    • From the start of the day after the collect-by date, in the shed's local time, the set-aside is no longer theirs: the tool goes to the next neighbor in the queue, or to whoever checks it out first if nobody is waiting (INV-CHK-3b, Check Out Tool). The hold drops off when Hold Expired is recorded.

Scenarios (Given / When / Then)

  • Hold placed (INV-MYHD-2, INV-MYHD-14, INV-MYHD-16)
    • Given: Tool Added was recorded for T1 "Cordless drill", Ana has T1 on loan, and nobody has a hold on it
    • When: Hold Placed is recorded for Ben's hold H1 on T1
    • Then: Ben's My Holds lists H1: "Cordless drill", waiting, position 1, pickup notice none, with Cancel offered.
  • A second hold placed (INV-MYHD-2)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is at position 1 on T1
    • When: Hold Placed is recorded for Cara's hold H2 on T1
    • Then: Cara's My Holds lists H2, waiting, position 2. Ben's is unchanged.
  • Holds placed in the same instant (INV-MYHD-2)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is at position 1 on T1
    • When: Hold Placed is recorded for Cara's H2 and then Dan's H3 on T1, with the same placedAt
    • Then: H2 is at position 2 and H3 at position 3: the order recorded decides, not placedAt.
  • Hold cancelled (INV-MYHD-6, INV-MYHD-2)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is at position 1 and Cara's H2 at position 2 on T1
    • When: Hold Cancelled is recorded for H1
    • Then: H1 drops off Ben's My Holds. Cara's H2 is at position 1.
  • Hold fulfilled (INV-MYHD-3, INV-MYHD-2)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is at position 1 and Cara's H2 at position 2 on T1, and T1 has been returned
    • When: Hold Fulfilled is recorded for H1, with the collect-by date 17 October
    • Then: Ben's My Holds shows H1 ready-for-pickup, collect by 17 October, with no position. Cara's H2 is at position 1.
  • Pickup email sent (INV-MYHD-13)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is ready-for-pickup, pickup notice none
    • When: Pickup Notice Sent is recorded for H1
    • Then: H1 shows pickup notice sent.
  • Pickup email couldn't be delivered (INV-MYHD-13)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is ready-for-pickup, collect by 17 October, pickup notice sent
    • When: Pickup Notice Failed is recorded for H1
    • Then: H1 shows pickup notice undelivered, still ready-for-pickup, collect by 17 October.
  • Collect-by date is the last day (INV-MYHD-17)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is ready-for-pickup, collect by 17 October
    • When: his holds are listed at 23:59 on 17 October, shed time
    • Then: H1 is ready-for-pickup.
  • Pickup window ended, not yet expired (INV-MYHD-17, INV-MYHD-16)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is ready-for-pickup, collect by 17 October, and Hold Expired hasn't been recorded
    • When: his holds are listed at 00:00 on 18 October, shed time
    • Then: H1 shows pickup-window-ended, with Cancel still offered.
  • Hold expired (INV-MYHD-4)
    • Given: Ben's H1 shows pickup-window-ended, and Cara's H2 is at position 1
    • When: Hold Expired is recorded for H1
    • Then: H1 drops off Ben's My Holds. Cara's H2 stays waiting at position 1 until Hold Fulfilled is recorded for it.
  • Suspended holder (INV-MYHD-3, INV-MYHD-11)
    • Given: Ben is suspended, and his H1 is at position 1 on T1
    • When: T1 is returned and Hold Fulfilled is recorded for H1, collect by 17 October
    • Then: Ben's My Holds shows H1 ready-for-pickup, collect by 17 October.
  • Holder collects the tool (INV-MYHD-5)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is ready-for-pickup, and Cara's H2 is at position 1
    • When: Tool Checked Out is recorded for T1 and Ben
    • Then: H1 drops off Ben's My Holds. Cara's is unchanged.
  • Front holder collects before the set-aside is recorded (INV-MYHD-5, INV-MYHD-2)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is at position 1 and Cara's H2 at position 2 on T1, and T1 has just been returned
    • When: Tool Checked Out is recorded for T1 and Ben, before Hold Fulfilled
    • Then: H1 drops off Ben's My Holds. Cara's H2 is at position 1.
  • Ready-for-pickup hold cancelled (INV-MYHD-6)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is ready-for-pickup, and Cara's H2 is at position 1
    • When: Hold Cancelled is recorded for H1
    • Then: H1 drops off Ben's My Holds. Cara's H2 stays waiting until Hold Fulfilled is recorded for it.
  • Tool retired (INV-MYHD-7)
    • Given: Ben's H1 and Cara's H2 are on T1
    • When: Tool Retired is recorded for T1
    • Then: H1 and H2 drop off both neighbors' My Holds.
  • Tool recorded lost (INV-MYHD-7)
    • Given: Ana has T1 on loan as loan L1, and Ben's H1 and Cara's H2 are on T1
    • When: Tool Lost is recorded for L1, the loan of T1
    • Then: H1 and H2 drop off both neighbors' My Holds.
  • Holder closes their account (INV-MYHD-8)
    • Given: Ben's H1 is at position 1 and Cara's H2 at position 2 on T1
    • When: Neighbor Account Closed is recorded for Ben
    • Then: H1 drops off. Cara's H2 is at position 1.
  • Hold again after expiry (INV-MYHD-2)
    • Given: Ben's H1 expired, and T1 is now set aside for Cara's H2
    • When: Hold Placed is recorded for Ben's new hold H4 on T1
    • Then: Ben's My Holds lists H4, waiting, position 1, behind Cara's set-aside.
  • Checkout by a neighbor with no hold (INV-MYHD-11)
    • Given: Ana has no holds, and the hammer (T5) is available
    • When: Tool Checked Out is recorded for T5 and Ana
    • Then: no neighbor's My Holds changes.
  • Only their own holds (INV-MYHD-1)
    • Given: Ben has H1 and Cara has H2, both on T1
    • When: Ben's holds are listed
    • Then: only H1 is returned, with its position. Nothing about H2 or Cara is returned.
  • Same event applied twice (INV-MYHD-15)
    • Given: Ben's My Holds lists H1 at position 1
    • When: the same Hold Placed for H1 is applied again
    • Then: Ben's My Holds still lists H1 once, at position 1, and no later hold's position changes.

Alternate & Error Flows

  • Repeated events: every event is applied idempotently (INV-MYHD-15). An event applied a second time leaves the view as it was after the first.
  • Events for a hold that has ended: once a hold has ended it is gone from this view. A later event for it (a replay, or a Pickup Notice Failed that arrives after the set-aside ended) changes nothing.
  • Unknown tool name: every hold's tool was added before it could be held, so Tool Added always precedes Hold Placed for the same tool.
  • Stale actions: Cancel offered on the screen can be out of date by the time it is used (for example, just as the hold expires or the tool is collected). Cancel Hold checks its own rules and refuses with its own reason; this view raises no errors of its own.

Non-Functional Requirements

  • Security / authz: a neighbor may list only their own holds (INV-MYHD-1). How the system knows which neighbor is asking is the open identity question below; until it is answered, nothing stops a caller asking for another neighbor ID.
  • PII & compliance: shows a neighbor their own holds only, and never who else holds or has a tool. The other holders and borrowers it keeps for working out positions are never returned.
  • Performance / SLA: none beyond the freshness above.

Dependencies & Read Models Affected

  • Upstream events this slice relies on, and the fields it reads from each:
    • Tool Added (Add Tool): toolId, name.
    • Hold Placed (Place Hold): holdId, toolId, neighborId, placedAt.
    • Hold Cancelled (Cancel Hold): holdId.
    • Hold Fulfilled (Fulfill Hold): holdId, collectByDate.
    • Pickup Notice Sent (Send Pickup Notice): holdId.
    • Pickup Notice Failed (Record Pickup Notice Failure): holdId.
    • Hold Expired (Expire Hold): holdId.
    • Tool Checked Out (Check Out Tool): loanId, toolId, neighborId.
    • Tool Retired (Retire Tool): toolId.
    • Tool Lost (Record Tool Lost): loanId, toolId. This view matches it by toolId.
    • Neighbor Account Closed (Close Account): neighborId.
    • Tool Added, Hold Placed and Tool Checked Out match slices/add-tool.md, slices/place-hold.md and slices/check-out-tool.md. The others are specified in slices not yet written in depth; these keys are this view's assumptions, and each is checked when that slice is.
  • Downstream read models / slices affected: none. The screen it feeds issues Cancel Hold.

Open Questions

  • How does the system know which neighbor is asking, so My Holds shows their holds and no one else's?
    • The same identity question is open in Add Tool, Register Neighbor, My Account, My Loans and Place Hold.
    • Options: (a) callers say who they are, and nothing checks it; (b) a sign-in outside the model supplies the neighbor's ID; (c) sign-in is modeled as events and slices.
    • Recommendation: (b), which adds nothing to the model.
  • In what order are holds listed?
    • This is the shed-wide question of one order for every list view: by name, then by when the item was created. For this view that means by tool name, then by when the hold was placed.
    • Recommendation: yes, that order.
